DETAILED ACTION
Notice of Pre-AIA  or AIA  Status
The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA .
Information Disclosure Statement
The information disclosure statement (IDS) submitted on 02/14/2023 was considered by the examiner.
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 102
The following is a quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for the rejections under this section made in this Office action:
A person shall be entitled to a patent unless –
(a)(1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
Claims 1, 2, 5, 10, 11, 12, and 15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Douglas US10487497.
Claim 1. Douglas discloses a sealing device for sealing an edge joint (1, Fig.3A) between cladding (12) of drywall and an adjacent floor, wall, or ceiling, the sealing device comprising: a one-piece sealing profile (1, Fig.1) comprising a bearing web (4) which is opposite a circumferential side of the cladding, a fastening web (2, Fig.1) running parallel to the bearing web that fastens the sealing profile to a holding rail of the drywall and an outer supporting web (3), viewed in cross section, covering the edge joint at least in portions, wherein the outer supporting web is adjacent to and supports the bearing web (4) and via which the bearing web is connected to the fastening web.
Claim 2. Douglas discloses wherein the fastening web, viewed in cross section, runs on the side remote from the outer supporting web further outward than the bearing web and forms the a portion of the sealing profile that extends furthest outward on the side remote from the outer supporting web (See 2 in Fig.1).
Claim 5. Douglas discloses the outer supporting web runs perpendicular to the bearing web (see 3 in Fig.1).
Claim 10 and 11. Douglas discloses the sealing profile is formed from a metal or a plastic material and is an extrusion profile (Col.8:48-65).
Claim 12. Douglas discloses the cladding presses with the circumferential side against the bearing web and the fastening web is held in a gap between the holding rail and the adjacent floor, wall, or ceiling (Fig.3A).
Claim 15. Douglas discloses producing drywall having a holding rail (6, Fig.3A), cladding (12), and a sealing device (1) according to claim1, the method comprising attaching the holding rail (6) to the floor (8), wall, and/or, ceiling, driving the fastening web (2) into a gap between the holding rail (8) and the adjacent floor, wall, or ceiling, so that the fastening web is clamped between the holding rail and the adjacent floor, wall, or ceiling, and fastening the cladding to a stand construction of the drywall, wherein the cladding rests with its the circumferential side against the bearing web (4).
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 103
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 103 which forms the basis for all obviousness rejections set forth in this Office action:
A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained, notwithstanding that the claimed invention is not identically disclosed as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.
Claims 3 and 4 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Douglas US10487497 as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Promat EP3584381.
Claim 3 and 4. Douglas is silent on the sealing profile has an inner supporting web which extends perpendicular to the bearing web up to the fastening web wherein the outer supporting web and the inner supporting web extend from opposite ends of the bearing web, viewed in cross section.
Promat before the filing date of the instant invention discloses a sealing device with the sealing profile has an inner supporting web which extends perpendicular to the bearing web up to the fastening web wherein the outer supporting web and the inner supporting web extend from opposite ends of the bearing web, viewed in cross section (see 312 of Fig.3B). It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the filing date of the instant invention to modify the device of Douglas with that of Promat for an improved seal as suggested by Promat, as a person with ordinary skill has good reason to pursue known options within his or her technical grasp.
Claims 3 and 4 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Douglas US10487497 as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Pilz US20140175386.
Claim 8. Douglas is silent a functional element made of an intumescent and/or sound-absorbing material is arranged in an interior  of the sealing profile and is fastened to the sealing profile. Pilz before the filing date of the instant invention discloses adding a functional element made of an intumescent to a sealing device. It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the filing date of the instant invention to modify the device of Douglas with that of Pilz with the motivation of stopping or reducing fire, as a person with ordinary skill has good reason to pursue known options within his or her technical grasp.
Allowable Subject Matter
Claims  objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.
The following is a statement of reasons for the indication of allowable subject matter: the closest prior art of record fails to teach or adequately suggest the combination of characteristics specified in the independent claim, especially the requirement of a substance concerning, hence there is no cogent reasoning that is unequivocally independent of hindsight that would have led one of ordinary skill in the art at the time.
Conclusion
The prior art made of record and not relied upon is considered pertinent to applicant's disclosure. Refer to attached NOTICE OF REFERENCE CITED.
